mainEntity.name: How do I calculate board feet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply thickness in inches by width in inches by length in feet, then divide by 12. A 2 × 4 that is 8 feet long is 2 × 4 × 8 ÷ 12 = 5.33 board feet.

mainEntity.name: Do I use nominal or actual sizes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lumber is priced on the nominal size, so a 2 × 4 counts as 2 × 4 inches even though it measures 1.5 × 3.5 inches. Hardwood is priced on its rough thickness in quarters. This tool follows those trade conventions.

mainEntity.name: How much waste should I allow?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 10% for clean, straight stock and 15% for typical work. Rustic or knotty boards, short cut-offs and complex joinery can push it to 25% or more.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between board feet and linear feet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Linear feet count only length. Board feet count volume, so a wide thick board has more board feet than a narrow thin one of the same length.

mainEntity.name: How many board feet are in a cubic foot?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are 12 board feet in a cubic foot, because a cubic foot is 1,728 cubic inches and a board foot is 144.
